title: IIS W3C log to ECS parser
brief:
In this repository, implement `parseIisLog(text)` in `src/iis.js`. It takes the full text of an IIS W3C extended log file and returns an array of ECS-style objects, one per request line.

Rules:
1. Lines starting with `#` are directives. `#Fields:` defines the column order for the lines that follow; a file may contain several `#Fields:` lines and each applies until the next one. Other directives are ignored. Blank lines are ignored.
2. Columns are separated by single spaces. A value of `-` means absent: omit that key entirely.
3. Map fields: `date`+`time` -> `@timestamp` as ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (e.g. `2026-10-01T08:15:02.000Z`); `s-ip` -> `server.ip`; `c-ip` -> `client.ip`; `cs-method` -> `http.request.method`; `cs-uri-stem` -> `url.path`; `cs-uri-query` -> `url.query`; `sc-status` -> `http.response.status_code` (number); `time-taken` (milliseconds) -> `event.duration` in nanoseconds (number); `cs(User-Agent)` -> `user_agent.original` with every `+` replaced by a space; `cs-username` -> `user.name`; `s-port` -> `server.port` (number). Unknown fields are ignored.
4. Output uses nested objects (`{ http: { request: { method: 'GET' } } }`), not dotted keys.
5. Lines whose column count does not match the active `#Fields:` are skipped. Lines before any `#Fields:` are skipped.

Keep the existing export name and ES module format. Run `npm test` to check the visible tests; you may add tests.
